headline: Goldman Sachs strategists say the AI investment story is splitting into a US-led and a China-led ecosystem with the technology gap narrowing, so Chinese AI stocks should be sorted into two groups.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the Goldman note is dated Sunday 11 Oct 2026, before the window, though Business Insider reported it on 13 Oct.
importance_line: What changed is that a major bank now treats Chinese AI shares as a separate market from US ones, which matters first to savers and pension holders whose funds hold either, then to governments weighing technology and export rules, then to AI companies in both camps, and the doubt is that it is one bank's strategy note, not a forecast of returns.
summary: Business Insider reports that Goldman Sachs strategists led by Kinger Lau wrote in a note published on Sunday 11 Oct 2026 that investors increasingly see a global AI duopoly, one ecosystem around the US and its key trading partners and another in China, and that the technology gaps between China and the West "seem to be narrowing". Goldman now splits Chinese AI stocks into exporters tied to Western AI spending, which gained 126% from early 2025 to June 2026 before falling 23% from their peak in the global AI selloff, and domestic firms, which have held up better, and says AI-related stocks now make up 42% of the combined value of Chinese shares listed in mainland China and Hong Kong, up from 24% in 2024.
notes: Read in full on Business Insider. The Goldman note is dated 11 Oct 2026 (before the window), so freshness is a follow-up and the score is lowered by 1; the qa check will hold it as re-dated.
